### Fixed
- **The Hugging Face cache claim no longer fails the connectivity release under a `WaitForFirstConsumer` StorageClass** (giantswarm/agent-platform#483; follows #326; epic giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). With `components.modelServing` on, `modelServing.cache.pvc` (`hf-cache`) rendered as a release resource with no consumer of its own: the first predictor (or download Job) that mounts it is what Binds it, so under kind's `standard` and the fleet's default `gp3` it stayed `Pending`, helm-controller's wait counted it as not ready and the release failed on every install and upgrade (`timeout waiting for: [PersistentVolumeClaim/model-serving/hf-cache status: 'InProgress']`, five attempts, then stalled) — with `kserve-resources` before it and substrate, kagent, agent-manager and model-manager behind it. The claim is now **applied by a `post-install,post-upgrade` hook Job** (`templates/model-serving/cache-pvc.yaml`; the chart's hook include and its identity `<release>-hooks`, whose ClusterRole carries `get`, `create`, `patch` on `persistentvolumeclaims` while the claim is the chart's — never `delete`): `kubectl apply --server-side` under the field manager `agent-platform-connectivity`, the log says `created` or `present` and the phase, and nothing waits for the claim to Bind — it binds where its first consumer schedules, which is what a zonal volume needs (the GPU pool's zone). The applied spec is the one the chart rendered (`hf-cache` in the serving namespace, `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`, `accessModes`, `size`, `storageClassName` incl. `"-"`, `volumeName`), and so is what a `cache.enabled` flip or an uninstall does — the claim stays, now because it is not Helm's. An installation upgrading from a chart that rendered the claim keeps it (the keep policy) and the hook takes its fields over (`--force-conflicts`); a size change is applied by the next upgrade's hook (the StorageClass has to allow expansion); an immutable field (`storageClassName`, `accessModes`, `volumeName`) fails the hook naming it. Installations without the switch render byte-identically (`make verify-modes`); `make verify-serving-slice` asserts the hook, its claim and identity, the knobs, and that `cache.enabled: false` or an `existingClaim` render none of it; `make verify-wiring` the serving shape without a `PersistentVolumeClaim` object; `make verify-gpu-pool` compares both sides without the claim. Not taken: a consumer pod of the chart's own (it would pin a zonal volume to its own zone and hold an RWO claim), an `Immediate`-binding class (the same zone lottery, and not the fleet's default), a release-wide `disableWait` (blind to the platform's dependency chain).
